clue.text: Very large vehicles gaining awards

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
cars are vehicles

explanation.surface: Giant vehicles winning prizes, perhaps at a motor show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Awards for film are popularly known by the name of their statuette.

clue.text: Parody about life initially makes us cross

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the parody wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a satire is a parody or send-up

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word life

explanation.surface: A send-up of life makes people angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes us' is a link phrase; 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: In fact, Edison appeared on stage

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A claim that the inventor Thomas Edison once performed in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acted is to have performed in a play, appearing before an audience.

clue.text: Suspect something's amiss, with master criminal holding everything up

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters wrap round the other piece
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of master are bent into a new order
in a down clue, up means the word for everything is read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A detective senses trouble as a criminal mastermind delays the whole operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master criminal' reads as a supervillain, but 'criminal' is the anagram signal working on master alone; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for growing suspicious that something underhand is going on.

clue.text: One's lair, in peace, in local

indicators.note: in places the first pair of pieces inside the word for peace

parts.note: rest is peace and quiet
one is the Roman numeral I
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Someone describes their quiet hideaway in a neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is someone who lives in a place, so it is an inhabitant or resident in the noun sense.

clue.text: Rebuke salesman over cover

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
a roof is a cover for a building

explanation.surface: A manager tells off a salesman about something to do with insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a scolding, the same as a rebuke given in words.

clue.text: Shoot any number out of season

indicators.note: out of means the letter for any number is removed from the season

parts.note: spring is a season
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: Advice to shoot any amount of game outside the permitted season.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

clue.text: Very attractive man met aboard at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone met a handsome man on board ship during a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is slang for a strikingly handsome, desirable person.

clue.text: Love recording with husband inside

indicators.note: inside means the husband's letter goes within the other word

parts.note: noting is recording, as in writing down

explanation.surface: Someone loves a recording made with their husband present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'Love' is the tennis score of zero, not affection.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring love means a score of zero, which is nil.

clue.text: No need for a prompt on stage if this character gets tense

definitions.text: No need for a prompt on stage

parts.note: a letter is a character of the alphabet
the perfect is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: An actor who knows their lines needs no prompter if the character comes over as nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective about the character's nerves but is the grammatical term; 'if this' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who knows every word of the script has no need of a prompter.

clue.text: 'Beefy' fare perhaps for riotous do in Oval

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rowdy party at the Oval, the London cricket ground, serves hearty food.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; 'Beefy' was the nickname of cricketer Ian Botham, and a beef curry is a hot dish. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery Indian curry, often made with beef, is an example of hearty fare.

clue.text: Stratagem revealed by doctor during walk

indicators.note: during means the doctor's letters fall in the middle of the walk

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor's cunning plan comes to light while out on a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening ploy, like a chess sacrifice, designed to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Tricky question: given time to relax, start to reply

parts.note: to ease is to relax

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word reply

explanation.surface: A tough question: given time to relax, begin answering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or brain-teaser that is hard to work out.

clue.text: Select cap randomly from display

indicators.note: randomly means the letters are picked out in no set order

explanation.surface: Choosing a hat at random from a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking show or display that draws the eye.

clue.text: Leave last from chateau encircled by French lake

indicators.note: encircled by means the chosen letter sits inside the abbreviation for French
last from points to the final letter of the word chateau

parts.note: lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a French chateau to stay by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlough is a leave of absence, especially for soldiers or workers.

clue.text: Fish reportedly studied on Hebridean island by English leader of team

indicators.note: reportedly tells us to go by how the word sounds rather than its spelling

parts.note: studied means read, past tense
Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A fish species was researched on a Scottish island by an English team leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of read rhymes with bed. 'on' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a Mediterranean food fish with a pinkish skin.

clue.text: Unsophisticated, eat sloppily and drink

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced

indicators.note: sloppily means done carelessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naive person eats messily and has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves make a pale brew popular in China and Japan.

clue.text: Sharp reply about employing one on job

indicators.note: employing means using, so the word for about takes in the other pieces

parts.note: re means about or concerning
one is the Roman numeral I
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A curt answer concerning hiring someone for a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link joining one to job.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, witty retort, originally a counter-thrust in fencing.

clue.text: Everybody catching salmon in the drink?

indicators.note: catching means the word for everybody holds the fish inside it

parts.note: all means everybody
coho is a species of Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: Everyone landing a salmon that has fallen into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' suggests the sea; 'the drink' is liquor. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is booze, the intoxicating drink in general.

clue.text: Row involving Greek character put in jail

indicators.note: involving means the noise wraps round the Greek letter

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person caught up in a quarrel ends up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to hold someone in custody, keeping them locked up.

clue.text: Understanding of current things in variety

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in variety means the letters appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Grasping today's events in all their diversity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'current' suggests up-to-date but is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding of a situation or person.

clue.text: Precisely what's required in old golf club, with foremost from Turnberry being entertained

indicators.note: being entertained means the chosen letter is a guest inside the club

parts.note: a spoon was an old wooden golf club, like a modern three wood

indicators.note: foremost from means the first letter of the word Turnberry

explanation.surface: An old golf club from the Turnberry course in Scotland is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnberry is a famous Scottish golf course. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on means exactly right, hitting the target perfectly.

clue.text: Not one tenor in group of singers

parts.note: none means not one

explanation.surface: Not a single tenor is in the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine performers or a piece for nine voices.

clue.text: Knowing 8, such a crossword can't be solved?

definitions.meaning: knowing the answer to 8 down, the word for zero, means having no idea at all

definitions.text: such a crossword can't be solved?
definitions.meaning: a puzzle with no clues in it could never be worked out

explanation.walkthrough: 8 down gives the word for zero, so knowing it is knowing nothing; the second reading splits the word into its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means ignorant, and literally a puzzle lacking any clues.

clue.text: Boy stopped by Irish landowner

indicators.note: stopped by means the abbreviation for Irish plugs the middle of the boy

parts.note: lad means boy

explanation.surface: A youngster is halted by an Irish landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner with a substantial estate.

clue.text: Ali had what Oliver wanted?

definitions.meaning: the boxer Muhammad Ali had seconds in his corner, assisting between rounds
Oliver Twist famously asked for more food in the workhouse

explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, seconds are the corner team who help the fighter; Dickens's Oliver Twist asked for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A further portion of food at a meal, which Oliver asked for, and assistance from seconds in the ring.

clue.text: Base of statue may be newly plastered right away

indicators.note: newly means made afresh, so the letters are put in a new order
away means the letter for right is taken out

explanation.surface: A statue's base could be freshly rendered straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately but means remove R; PLASTEED (PLASTERED without R) is rearranged by 'newly'. 'may be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the plinth or base on which a statue stands.

clue.text: Until now gallery has accepted what's bizarre, without limit

indicators.note: has accepted means the gallery takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: without limit means the end letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: odd means bizarre

explanation.surface: An art gallery has so far taken in strange work without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery; 'has accepted' is the containment signal and 'without limit' trims the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is an idiom meaning so far, up to the present time.
